sections.title: Frontier Model as Direct Policy
sections.blurb: The general-purpose model itself emits the next action (end-effector pose, joint target, trajectory) at every step. No learned System 1 underneath; the only thing below it is IK / a position controller.

sections.title: Agentic & Code-Writing Policies
sections.blurb: The model acts through a harness: it writes and runs code against sensing/perception/motion APIs, observes the outcome, and repairs. Learned System 1 is absent; motion is analytic (IK, waypoints, ROS).

sections.title: Frontier Model over a Learned System 1 / System 0
sections.blurb: The general model supervises, steers, or edits the output of a learned low-level controller (a VLA, a world-action model, or a whole-body tracker). This is where the 'is System 1 still needed?' question is decided.

sections.title: Getting Better Without Weight Updates
sections.blurb: Memory, practice, skill libraries, and in-context learning: the general model improves across episodes while its weights stay frozen (or it trains a separate policy for you).

sections.title: Making It Fast & Cheap
sections.blurb: Latency and dollar cost are the main open problem. Distillation into small models, open-weight harnesses, asynchronous planning/execution. Thin on purpose: this is the research gap.

sections.title: The Incumbent: Dual-System VLAs
sections.blurb: The architecture being challenged. A VLM 'System 2' fused with a fast learned 'System 1' action module, plus the work on how training one damages the other.

sections.title: Benchmarks & Evaluation Reports
sections.blurb: Shared yardsticks where frontier models and learned policies are scored on the same tasks.

sections.title: Analyses, Critiques & Reproducibility
sections.blurb: Negative results, retests, benchmark-integrity problems, and the limits authors admit about their own systems.

sections.title: Surveys, Essays & Perspectives
sections.blurb: Big-picture framing: where System 2 ends, what System 1 / System 0 becomes, and what it means for the field.

sections.title: Foundations (pre-2025)
sections.blurb: The LLM-as-planner and code-as-policy lineage this area grew from.
